question: I wrote an event subscriber class in my plugin but Shopware never calls it. How do I register it correctly?
ground_truth: The class must implement Symfony's EventSubscriberInterface and return an event => method map from getSubscribedEvents(). It also has to be registered as a service in the plugin's src/Resources/config/services.php and tagged with kernel.event_subscriber; without that registration and tag Shopware never calls it.

question: Which bin/console commands install and activate a plugin I just created?
ground_truth: First run bin/console plugin:refresh so Shopware picks up the new plugin, then bin/console plugin:install --activate <PluginName> (e.g. SwagBasicExample) to install and activate it in one step.

question: How can I scaffold a new plugin from the CLI, and which files are always generated?
ground_truth: Run bin/console plugin:create <PluginName> from the project root (name in UpperCamelCase, ideally with a vendor prefix). It always generates composer.json, the plugin base class, config.xml, .gitignore and a PHPUnit setup. --static creates it in custom/static-plugins and --no-scaffold skips the optional example files.

question: Where does the config.xml for a plugin settings page go and what is the minimum it has to contain?
ground_truth: Create src/Resources/config/config.xml inside the plugin; the Administration renders it automatically. It must contain at least one <card> element with a <title> and at least one <input-field> (with a <name>).

question: How do I read a value from my plugin's configuration inside a PHP service?
ground_truth: Inject Shopware\Core\System\SystemConfig\SystemConfigService and call get() with the prefixed key <BundleName>.config.<fieldName>, e.g. $systemConfigService->get('SwagBasicExample.config.example', $salesChannelId). The prefix avoids collisions between plugins that use the same field name.

question: What classes and service tags do I need to create a scheduled task in a plugin?
ground_truth: A task class extending ScheduledTask that implements getTaskName() (vendor-prefixed technical name) and getDefaultInterval() (interval in seconds), and a handler extending ScheduledTaskHandler with #[AsMessageHandler(handles: ExampleTask::class)] whose run() method contains the logic. In services.php the task is tagged shopware.scheduled.task and the handler messenger.message_handler. Tasks are registered on plugin install/update or via bin/console scheduled-task:register.

question: How do I add my own command to bin/console from a plugin?
ground_truth: Write a standard Symfony Console command (a class extending Command, e.g. with #[AsCommand(name: 'swag:example')]) and register it as a service in src/Resources/config/services.php tagged with console.command. It is then available via bin/console.

question: How can I change what an existing core service does without touching core code?
ground_truth: Use service decoration: register your decorator in services.php with ->decorate(OriginalService::class) and pass service('.inner') as argument. The decorator extends the service's abstract class (e.g. AbstractExampleService), receives the original service in its constructor and returns it from getDecorated(). It should call the inner service so other decorators and the core logic still run.

question: What should my plugin's uninstall method do when the merchant wants to keep the plugin data?
ground_truth: uninstall() receives an UninstallContext. If $context->keepUserData() returns true, the plugin must not delete its persistent data and should return early; otherwise it can clean up. Even then, entities still referenced elsewhere (e.g. a payment method used in orders) should not be blindly deleted.

question: How do I create a database migration for my plugin and which method should contain the schema changes?
ground_truth: Generate it with bin/console database:create-migration -p <PluginName> --name <Description>. This creates a Migration<timestamp><Description> class extending MigrationStep with getCreationTimestamp() and update(). All schema and data changes go into update(); updateDestructive() is never executed on plugin install or update.

question: My plugin needs an extra PHP library from Packagist. How do I add it so it also works when the plugin is installed from a zip?
ground_truth: Require the package in the plugin's composer.json (temporarily remove shopware/core from require while running composer require so Shopware itself is not downloaded into vendor, then add it back). For zip-installed plugins either ship the vendor directory in the bundle (max 5 MB) or override executeComposerCommands() in the plugin base class to return true so Shopware runs Composer during installation.

question: How do I give my plugin its own log channel?
ground_truth: Configure Monolog in the plugin (src/Resources/config/packages/monolog.yaml) with channels: ['my_plugin_channel']. Monolog then registers a logger scoped to that channel with the service id monolog.logger.my_plugin_channel, which can be injected, and a handler can direct the channel to its own output.

question: How can I pass extra data from my plugin to a storefront pagelet like the footer and show it in Twig?
ground_truth: Subscribe to the pagelet's loaded event (e.g. FooterPageletLoadedEvent) in an event subscriber tagged kernel.event_subscriber, and attach the data with $event->getPagelet()->addExtension('product_count', $data). In the template the data is available under the extensions key, e.g. footer.extensions.product_count.

question: How do I define a custom entity for my own database table with the DAL?
ground_truth: Create a class extending EntityDefinition with an ENTITY_NAME constant, getEntityName() returning the table name (also used for the <name>.repository service) and defineFields() returning a FieldCollection. Register it in services.php with the shopware.entity.definition tag. Custom Entity and EntityCollection classes are recommended (wired via getEntityClass()/getCollectionClass()); the table itself is created by a migration.

question: How do I fetch products by name using the product repository?
ground_truth: Create a Criteria, add an EqualsFilter on the name field, e.g. $criteria->addFilter(new EqualsFilter('name', 'Example name')), and call $productRepository->search($criteria, $context); use ->first() or getEntities() on the result.

question: I want to load products together with only their reviews that have at least 4 points. How do I filter the association?
ground_truth: Use $criteria->getAssociation('productReviews')->addFilter(new RangeFilter('points', [RangeFilter::GTE => 4])). getAssociation returns a Criteria for the association, so the filter limits which reviews are loaded. Filtering on productReviews.points with addFilter on the main criteria would instead filter the products themselves.

question: When should I use addPostFilter instead of addFilter on a Criteria?
ground_truth: Use addPostFilter when the filter should restrict the returned result but must not apply to aggregations, e.g. return only products named 'Example product' while aggregations/totals still consider all products.

question: How can I write an entity so that it is created if missing and updated if it already exists?
ground_truth: Use the repository's upsert() method and provide the ID in the data; the DAL then updates the entity if it exists or creates it otherwise.

question: How do I add my own field to the existing product entity from a plugin?
ground_truth: Create a class extending EntityExtension, add fields in extendFields(FieldCollection $collection) and return the extended entity's name (product) from getEntityName(); register it tagged shopware.entity.extension. You must not add columns to the product table - store data in your own table linked e.g. via a OneToOneAssociationField. BulkEntityExtension extends several entities at once.

question: How do I compute the average review rating of products with a DAL aggregation?
ground_truth: Add the association and an AvgAggregation to the criteria, e.g. $criteria->addAggregation(new AvgAggregation('avg-rating', 'productReviews.points')), run search() and read $result->getAggregations()->get('avg-rating') from the EntitySearchResult (not from first()).

question: How do I override a block of the storefront header logo template in my plugin?
ground_truth: Mirror the core path inside the plugin: src/Resources/views/storefront/layout/header/logo.html.twig, extend the original with {% sw_extends '@Storefront/storefront/layout/header/logo.html.twig' %} and redefine the block. Use {{ parent() }} inside the block to append to the original content instead of replacing it.

question: What are the steps to create a new theme and assign it to my sales channel?
ground_truth: Run bin/console theme:create <ThemeName> (e.g. SwagBasicExampleTheme), install and activate the generated plugin, assign the theme to the sales channel with bin/console theme:change and compile it with bin/console theme:compile. The theme is configured in its theme.json.

question: How do I override Bootstrap SCSS variables such as $border-radius in my theme?
ground_truth: Add the overrides.scss entry point (app/storefront/src/scss/overrides.scss) to the style array in theme.json before @Storefront, set the variables there (e.g. $border-radius: 0) and run bin/console theme:compile.

question: How do I register a storefront JavaScript plugin that only runs on elements with a specific data attribute?
ground_truth: Write a class extending PluginBaseClass and register it in src/Resources/app/storefront/src/main.js with PluginManager.register('ExamplePlugin', ExamplePlugin, '[data-example-plugin]'). It only runs where an element with that attribute exists (this.el is the element); a dynamic import() can be passed to load the plugin asynchronously.

question: How do I add a custom storefront route with its own controller and template?
ground_truth: Create a controller extending StorefrontController with the route scope set via #[Route(defaults: [PlatformRequest::ATTRIBUTE_ROUTE_SCOPE => [StorefrontRouteScope::ID]])], define the action with e.g. #[Route(path: '/example', name: 'frontend.example.example', methods: ['GET'])] and return $this->renderStorefront('@SwagBasicExample/storefront/page/example.html.twig', [...]). Routes are loaded via a routes.php file in src/Resources/config.

question: I changed SCSS in my theme but nothing changes in the browser. Which command do I need to run?
ground_truth: Run bin/console theme:compile to rebuild the theme assets (in watch mode the variables are injected dynamically instead).

question: How does a backend integration get an access token for the Admin API?
ground_truth: Create an integration in the Administration (Settings > System > Integrations). Its access key ID is the OAuth client_id and the secret access key the client_secret. POST them with grant_type client_credentials to /api/oauth/token and send the returned token as Authorization: Bearer <token> (it expires, e.g. expires_in 600).

question: Which header must a headless frontend send to authenticate against the Store API?
ground_truth: The sw-access-key header containing the sales channel's API access key (found in the sales channel's API access section). The sw-context-token header additionally identifies the customer's context/session.

question: How do I create my own Store API endpoint in a plugin?
ground_truth: Create an abstract route class (e.g. AbstractExampleRoute) with getDecorated() and load(Criteria, SalesChannelContext). Implement it in ExampleRoute with the store-api route scope (#[Route(defaults: [PlatformRequest::ATTRIBUTE_ROUTE_SCOPE => [StoreApiRouteScope::ID]])]) and a #[Route(path: '/store-api/example', ...)] on load(); getDecorated() throws DecorationPatternException. The response class extends StoreApiResponse.

question: How can I change the response of an existing Store API route from my plugin?
ground_truth: Decorate the route: create a class extending the route's abstract class (e.g. ExampleRouteDecorator extends AbstractExampleRoute), inject the original route, return it from getDecorated(), and in load() call the decorated route and adjust or replace the result. Register it as a decorator of the original route.

question: How do I send a search request with filters to the Admin API, for example only active products?
ground_truth: Send a POST request with the criteria as a JSON object to the entity's search endpoint (e.g. /api/search/product), with a filter array such as {"type": "equals", "field": "active", "value": true}; the same criteria supports page/limit, associations, includes, sort, aggregations and total-count-mode.

question: How can I make the API return only a few fields of an entity, and how is that different from includes?
ground_truth: Use partial data loading by passing a fields list in the criteria (e.g. "fields": ["name"]); only those fields are loaded, and fields of associations can be referenced. includes is post-output processing: the full entity is loaded and only the response is filtered. Some fields such as id and foreign keys are always loaded.

question: Which request header selects the language in which entities are returned by the API?
ground_truth: The sw-language-id header with the ID of the language; without it the API uses the system language (falling back to it when a translation is missing).

question: How should the message queue be processed on a production server?
ground_truth: Run CLI workers such as bin/console messenger:consume async low_priority with limits like --time-limit=60 --memory-limit=128M, kept alive by a process manager (e.g. a systemd unit or supervisor). When CLI workers are used, disable the admin worker in shopware.yaml with shopware.admin_worker.enable_admin_worker: false.

question: How are scheduled tasks triggered on a production system?
ground_truth: Run bin/console scheduled-task:run together with a message queue worker (messenger:consume). Alternatively run scheduled-task:run --no-wait from cron (e.g. every 5 minutes), or consume the scheduler_shopware transport with bin/console messenger:consume scheduler_shopware.

question: How can I run one specific scheduled task right now for debugging, without the queue?
ground_truth: Use bin/console scheduled-task:run-single <task_name>, e.g. bin/console scheduled-task:run-single log_entry.cleanup.

question: Which environment variable turns Shopware's HTTP cache on or off?
ground_truth: SHOPWARE_HTTP_CACHE_ENABLED (default 1, i.e. enabled).

question: What is the expected format of the DATABASE_URL environment variable?
ground_truth: A DSN for MySQL/MariaDB in the form mysql://user:password@host:port/dbname.

question: How do I enable Elasticsearch/OpenSearch for the storefront search and build the index?
ground_truth: Set OPENSEARCH_URL to the host(s), SHOPWARE_ES_ENABLED=1 (use Elasticsearch for the shop) and SHOPWARE_ES_INDEXING_ENABLED=1 (enable indexing), then run bin/console es:index; some setups additionally need bin/console es:create:alias after indexing finishes.

question: Can I set system configuration values in YAML files so they override what is stored in the database?
ground_truth: Yes, with the static system configuration: create a file in config/packages (e.g. config/packages/<name>.yaml) with a shopware.system_config section. It is an overlay - the database configuration is loaded first and the static values overwrite it.

question: Can a Shopware app modify the database schema, and where can plugins versus apps run?
ground_truth: No - apps cannot modify the database schema; they communicate via HTTP APIs/webhooks and run externally, which makes them cloud-compatible. Plugins have full system access and can change the database structure, but are only available for self-hosted installations.

question: How do I change the cart at runtime, for example to add a custom discount line item?
ground_truth: Implement a cart collector (CartDataCollectorInterface with collect(), to fetch data) and/or a cart processor (CartProcessorInterface with process(), to modify the calculated cart) and register them as services with the corresponding cart tags.
